nodes.name: Supersymmetrization of GESM theories
nodes.statement:
The supersymmetrization of the
theories introduced in this paper is currently an open problem
involving several objects and structures of mathematical interest,
such as spinor bundles and Lipschitz structures, Special-K\"ahler and
Quaternionic-K\"ahler manifolds or exceptional Lie groups, all
interacting in a delicate equilibrium dictated by supersymmetry.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction
nodes.statement_short: Supersymmetrizing the theories introduced in the paper is open.

nodes.name: Standing smoothness assumptions
nodes.statement:
All manifolds considered are smooth, connected, Hausdorff and
paracompact (hence also second countable) while all fiber bundles
considered are smooth.

nodes.name: Hom and Isom bundles and their sections
nodes.statement:
Given vector bundles $\mathcal{S}$
and $\mathcal{S}'$ over some manifold $M$, we denote by $Hom(\mathcal{S},\mathcal{S}')$,
$Isom(\mathcal{S},\mathcal{S}')$ the bundles of morphisms and isomorphisms from $\mathcal{S}$
to $\mathcal{S}'$ and by ${\rm Hom}(\mathcal{S},\mathcal{S}')\stackrel{{\rm def.}}{=} \Gamma(M, Hom(\mathcal{S},\mathcal{S}'))$,
$\mathrm{Isom}(\mathcal{S},\mathcal{S}')\stackrel{{\rm def.}}{=} \Gamma(M, Isom(\mathcal{S},\mathcal{S}'))$ the sets of smooth
sections of these bundles.

Given a smooth map

By definition, a Lorentzian manifold is a

nodes.name: Path space P(M)

Given a
manifold $M$, let $\mathcal{P}(M)$ denote the set of paths (piecewise-smooth

nodes.name: Kaluza-Klein spaces as auxiliary data
nodes.statement:
Throughout the paper, we use the mathematical concept of
``Kaluza-Klein space'', which is well-established in the mathematics
and mathematical physics literature (see, for example,
\cite{Bourguignon,Hogan,Betounes1,Betounes2,Besse}). Such spaces were
initially defined and studied in the context of mathematical
foundations of Kaluza-Klein theories, which arise by reducing a
higher-dimensional theory of gravity on such a manifold. In the present
paper, such spaces are used merely as convenient auxiliary
mathematical data which parameterize a GESM theory, despite the
historical context in which they were introduced initially. Throughout
the paper, no reduction of any putative higher dimensional theory on
such spaces is ever suggested or performed.
nodes.section: 1.1 Notations and conventions

nodes.name: Space-time is a connected Lorentzian four-manifold
nodes.statement: Let $(M,g)$ be a connected four-dimensional Lorentzian manifold.
nodes.section: 2.1 Lorentzian submersions and Kaluza-Klein metrics

nodes.name: Total space of dimension n+4
nodes.statement:
Let
$E$ be a connected manifold of dimension $\dim E=n+4$, where $n>0$.
nodes.section: 2.1 Lorentzian submersions and Kaluza-Klein metrics

nodes.name: Surjective submersion
nodes.statement:
Recall that a smooth map $\pi:E\rightarrow M$ is called a {\em
  surjective submersion} if $\pi$ is surjective and the linear map
$\mathrm{d}_e \pi\colon T_e E\rightarrow T_{\pi(e)} M$ is surjective for all
$e\in E$.
nodes.section: 2.1 Lorentzian submersions and Kaluza-Klein metrics

nodes.name: Vertical distribution
nodes.statement:
The
{\em vertical distribution} of $\pi$ is the rank $n$ distribution
$V\stackrel{{\rm def.}}{=} \ker (\mathrm{d} \pi)\subset T E$ defined on $E$, which is Frobenius
integrable and integrates to the foliation whose leaves are the fibers
of $\pi$.
nodes.section: 2.1 Lorentzian submersions and Kaluza-Klein metrics
nodes.statement_short: V = ker(dpi), the rank-n integrable distribution tangent to the fibers.

nodes.name: pi-positive Lorentzian metric
nodes.statement:
A Lorentzian metric $h$ on $E$ is called {\em
  $\pi$-positive} if its restriction to each fiber of $\pi$ is
positive-definite.
nodes.section: 2.1 Lorentzian submersions and Kaluza-Klein metrics
differentia: its restriction to each fiber of $\pi$ is positive-definite

nodes.name: Horizontal distribution determined by h
nodes.statement:
In this case, the $h$-orthogonal complement
$H:=H(h)$ of $V$ inside $TE$ is a distribution of rank four called the
{\em horizontal distribution} of $\pi$ determined by $h$.
nodes.section: 2.1 Lorentzian submersions and Kaluza-Klein metrics

nodes.name: Vertical and horizontal metrics
nodes.statement:
Let $h_V$
and $h_H$ denote the metrics induced by $h$ on $V$ and $H$, which we
call the {\em vertical} and {\em horizontal} metrics induced by
$h$.
nodes.section: 2.1 Lorentzian submersions and Kaluza-Klein metrics

nodes.name: Horizontal isomorphism (d pi)_H
nodes.statement:
For any $e\in E$, the map $\mathrm{d}_e \pi$ restricts to a linear
bijection from $H_e$ to $T_{\pi(e)}M$. Hence the restriction
$\mathrm{d}\pi|_H$ of $\mathrm{d} \pi$ to $H$ induces a based isomorphism of vector
bundles $(\mathrm{d}\pi)_H\colon H\stackrel{\sim}{\rightarrow} (TM)^\pi$.
nodes.section: 2.1 Lorentzian submersions and Kaluza-Klein metrics

nodes.name: Lorentzian submersion
nodes.statement:
Let $h$ be a $\pi$-positive Lorentzian metric on $E$. 
The surjective submersion $\pi:E\rightarrow M$ is called a {\em
  Lorentzian submersion} from $(E,h)$ to $(M,g)$ if the bundle
isomorphism $(\mathrm{d}\pi)_H$ is an isometry from $(H,h_H)$ to
$((TM)^\pi,g^\pi)$.
nodes.section: 2.1 Lorentzian submersions and Kaluza-Klein metrics
differentia:
the
bundle isomorphism $(\mathrm{d}\pi)_H$ is an isometry from $(H,h_H)$ to
$((TM)^\pi,g^\pi)$

nodes.name: Signature of horizontal and vertical distributions
nodes.statement:
When $\pi$ is a Lorentzian submersion from $(E,h)$ to $(M,g)$, the
pair $(H,h_H)$ is a pseudo-Euclidean distribution of signature $(3,1)$
defined on $E$ while $(V,h_V)$ is a Euclidean distribution. In
particular, $\pi$ is a surjective pseudo-Riemannian submersion in the
sense of \cite{ONeillBook}.
nodes.section: 2.1 Lorentzian submersions and Kaluza-Klein metrics
assumptions: When $\pi$ is a Lorentzian submersion from $(E,h)$ to $(M,g)$
conclusions:
the
pair $(H,h_H)$ is a pseudo-Euclidean distribution of signature $(3,1)$
defined on $E$ while $(V,h_V)$ is a Euclidean distribution

$\pi$ is a surjective pseudo-Riemannian submersion in the
sense of \cite{ONeillBook}

nodes.name: Kaluza-Klein metric
nodes.statement:
A {\em Kaluza-Klein metric} for the surjective submersion
$\pi:E\rightarrow M$ relative to the Lorentzian metric $g\in
\mathrm{Met}_{3,1}(M)$ is a $\pi$-positive Lorentzian metric $h$ on $E$
which makes $\pi$ into a Lorentzian submersion from $(E,h)$ to
$(M,g)$.
nodes.section: 2.1 Lorentzian submersions and Kaluza-Klein metrics
differentia:
which makes $\pi$ into a Lorentzian submersion from $(E,h)$ to
$(M,g)$

nodes.name: Horizontal lift of vector fields
nodes.statement:
Any horizontal distribution $H$ defines a horizontal lift of vector
fields, which takes $Q\in \mathcal{X}(M)$ into the unique horizontal vector
field $\bar{Q}\in \Gamma(E,H)$ satisfying $\mathrm{d}\pi(\bar{Q}) = Q$.
nodes.section: 2.1 Lorentzian submersions and Kaluza-Klein metrics

nodes.name: Horizontal/vertical decomposition of vector fields
nodes.statement:
Moreover, 
any vector field $X\in \mathcal{X}(E)$ decomposes uniquely as $X=X_H\oplus X_V$, 
where $X_H\in \Gamma(E,H)$ and $X_V\in \Gamma(E,V)$.
nodes.section: 2.1 Lorentzian submersions and Kaluza-Klein metrics

nodes.name: Curvature equals O'Neill A-tensor up to a factor
nodes.section: 2.1 Lorentzian submersions and Kaluza-Klein metrics
nodes.statement_short: On horizontal vectors, F_H equals twice O'Neill's A tensor.
conclusions: A_XY=-A_YX=\frac{1}{2}\mathcal{F}_H(X,Y)

nodes.name: Vanishing of O'Neill's tensor
nodes.statement:
A basic property of O'Neill's tensor is that it vanishes if and only
if $\mathcal{F}_H$ does.
nodes.section: 2.1 Lorentzian submersions and Kaluza-Klein metrics
conclusions:
it vanishes if and only
if $\mathcal{F}_H$ does

nodes.name: Complete horizontal distribution
nodes.statement:
The distribution $H$ is called {\em complete} if the flow $T$ defined
by horizontal lifts of vector fields is globally-defined, which
amounts to the condition that {\em any} curve in $M$ lifts to a
horizontal curve in $E$ through any point lying in the fiber above its
source.
nodes.section: 2.1 Lorentzian submersions and Kaluza-Klein metrics

nodes.name: Ehresmann's theorem on complete connections
nodes.statement:
When $H$ is complete, it follows from a result of
\cite{Ehresmann} that $\pi$ is a fiber bundle, though its structure
group need not be a finite-dimensional Lie group.
nodes.section: 2.1 Lorentzian submersions and Kaluza-Klein metrics
conclusions: $\pi$ is a fiber bundle

nodes.name: Ehresmann connection and Ehresmann transport
nodes.statement:
In this case, $H$ is
an Ehresmann connection for $\pi$ and $T$ is called its Ehresmann
transport.
nodes.section: 2.1 Lorentzian submersions and Kaluza-Klein metrics

nodes.name: Reckziegel's fiber bundle theorem
nodes.statement:
Reference \cite{Reckziegel} shows that a sufficient
condition for $H$ to be complete and for the structure group to be a
finite-dimensional Lie group is that the fibers of $\pi$ be
geodesically complete and totally geodesic connected submanifolds of
$(E,h)$.
nodes.section: 2.1 Lorentzian submersions and Kaluza-Klein metrics
assumptions:
the fibers of $\pi$ be
geodesically complete and totally geodesic connected submanifolds of
$(E,h)$
conclusions:
$H$ to be complete and for the structure group to be a
finite-dimensional Lie group

nodes.name: Isometric Ehresmann transport
nodes.statement:
In this case the Ehresmann transport $T$ is isometric, which
means that $T_\gamma$ is an isometry from $E_{\gamma(0)}$ to
$E_{\gamma(1)}$ for any path $\gamma\in \mathcal{P}(M)$.
nodes.section: 2.1 Lorentzian submersions and Kaluza-Klein metrics

nodes.name: Structure group is the fiber isometry group
nodes.statement:
Hence the structure
group is isomorphic to the Riemannian isometry group of the fiber of
$\pi$ over any given point in $M$.
nodes.section: 2.1 Lorentzian submersions and Kaluza-Klein metrics

nodes.name: Lorentzian Kaluza-Klein space
nodes.statement:
A {\em Lorentzian Kaluza-Klein space} over $(M,g)$ is a Lorentzian
submersion $\pi:(E,h)\rightarrow (M,g)$ such that $(E,h)$ is connected
and such that the fibers of $\pi$ are geodesically complete and
totally geodesic connected submanifolds of $(E,h)$. The Kaluza-Klein
space is called {\em integrable} if the horizontal distribution
$H(h)\subset TE$ defined by $h$ is Frobenius integrable.
nodes.section: 2.2 Lorentzian Kaluza-Klein spaces
nodes.statement_short: A Lorentzian submersion with connected total space whose fibers are complete, totally geodesic and connected; integrable if H is.
differentia:
the fibers of $\pi$ are geodesically complete and
totally geodesic connected submanifolds of $(E,h)$

nodes.name: Model fiber (M,G)
nodes.statement:
Let $m_0$ be fixed point of $M$ and let $\mathcal{M}\stackrel{{\rm def.}}{=}
E_{m_0}=\pi^{-1}(\{m_0\})$ and $\mathcal{G}\stackrel{{\rm def.}}{=} h|_{E_{m_0}}$.
nodes.section: 2.2 Lorentzian Kaluza-Klein spaces

nodes.name: Proof that h is determined by g, G, H
nodes.statement:
As mentioned
above, the results of \cite{Reckziegel} imply that $H$ is a complete
Ehresmann connection, that $\pi$ is a fiber bundle and that the
transport $T$ is isometric. Hence the restriction $h_m\stackrel{{\rm def.}}{=} h|_{E_m}$
of $h$ to the fibers of $E$ is uniquely determined by $\mathcal{G}$ and by
$T$.
nodes.section: 2.2 Lorentzian Kaluza-Klein spaces
nodes.statement_short: Reckziegel's theorem makes transport isometric, so fiber metrics follow from G and T.

nodes.name: Kaluza-Klein metric determined by g, G and H
nodes.statement:
Therefore, the metric $h$ of a Kaluza-Klein space is uniquely
determined by $g$, $\mathcal{G}$ and $H$. When $g$ and $\mathcal{G}$ are fixed, we
thus have a bijection between Ehresmann connections $H$ for $\pi$ and
Lorentzian metrics $h$ on $E$ such that $\pi:(E,h)\rightarrow (M,g)$
is a Kaluza-Klein space and such that $h_{m_0}=\mathcal{G}$.
nodes.section: 2.2 Lorentzian Kaluza-Klein spaces
conclusions:
the metric $h$ of a Kaluza-Klein space is uniquely
determined by $g$, $\mathcal{G}$ and $H$

nodes.name: Ehresmann holonomy group
nodes.section: 2.2 Lorentzian Kaluza-Klein spaces

nodes.name: Holonomy bundle
nodes.statement:
For any $m\in M$, consider the set:
\begin{equation*}
\Pi_m \stackrel{{\rm def.}}{=} \{T_\gamma\,\, |\,\, \gamma\in \mathcal{P}(M): \gamma(0)=m_0\,\, \&\,\,  \gamma(1)=m\}\, ,
\end{equation*}
and let $\Pi\stackrel{{\rm def.}}{=} \sqcup_{m\in M}\Pi_m$ be endowed with the obvious
projection to $M$.  Then $\Pi$ is a principal $G$-bundle (known as the
{\em holonomy bundle} of $H$ relative to $m_0$) under the obvious
right action of $G$.
nodes.section: 2.2 Lorentzian Kaluza-Klein spaces
nodes.statement_short: Pi is the bundle of transports from m0 to m; a principal G-bundle.

nodes.name: Proof of the classification of Kaluza-Klein spaces
nodes.statement:
Moreover, the Ehresmann connection $H$ induces a
principal connection $\theta$ on $\Pi$. Conversely, let $\rho$ be the
isometric action of $G$ on $\mathcal{M}$ given by the inclusion $G\subseteq
\mathrm{Iso}(\mathcal{M},\mathcal{G})$. Then the associated bundle construction associates to
a principal bundle $\Pi$ with principal connection $\theta$ the fiber
bundle $E_\Pi\stackrel{{\rm def.}}{=} \Pi\times_\rho \mathcal{M}$ with induced Ehresmann
connection $H_\theta$. The two correspondences described above give
mutually quasi-inverse functors between the groupoid of Kaluza-Klein
spaces over $(M,g)$ which have typical fiber $(\mathcal{M},\mathcal{G})$ and are
endowed with a horizontal distribution $H$ with holonomy $G\subseteq
\mathrm{Iso}(\mathcal{M},\mathcal{G})$ and the groupoid of principal $G$-bundles $\Pi$ defined
over $M$ and endowed with a principal connection $\theta$ together
with an embedding $G\subseteq \mathrm{Iso}(\mathcal{M},\mathcal{G})$ up to conjugation. Hence:
nodes.section: 2.2 Lorentzian Kaluza-Klein spaces
nodes.statement_short: Construct mutually quasi-inverse functors: holonomy bundle with induced connection, and the associated bundle construction.

nodes.name: Classification of Kaluza-Klein spaces by principal bundles with connection
nodes.statement:
Let $g$ be a fixed Lorentzian metric on $M$. Then isomorphism classes
of Kaluza-Klein spaces over $(M,g)$ with typical fiber $(\mathcal{M},\mathcal{G})$ and
horizontal distribution $H$ having Ehresmann holonomy contained in
$\mathrm{Iso}(\mathcal{M},\mathcal{G})$ are in bijection with isomorphism classes of principal
$G$-bundles $\Pi$ defined over $M$ and endowed with a principal
connection $\theta$ whose holonomy is embedded in $\mathrm{Iso}(\mathcal{M},\mathcal{G})$. 
Moreover, $H$ is integrable if and only if $\theta$ is
flat.
nodes.section: 2.2 Lorentzian Kaluza-Klein spaces
nodes.statement_short: KK spaces with fiber (M,G) correspond to principal G-bundles with connection whose holonomy embeds in Iso(M,G); H integrable iff theta flat.
assumptions: Let $g$ be a fixed Lorentzian metric on $M$.
conclusions:
isomorphism classes
of Kaluza-Klein spaces over $(M,g)$ with typical fiber $(\mathcal{M},\mathcal{G})$ and
horizontal distribution $H$ having Ehresmann holonomy contained in
$\mathrm{Iso}(\mathcal{M},\mathcal{G})$ are in bijection with isomorphism classes of principal
$G$-bundles $\Pi$ defined over $M$ and endowed with a principal
connection $\theta$ whose holonomy is embedded in $\mathrm{Iso}(\mathcal{M},\mathcal{G})$

$H$ is integrable if and only if $\theta$ is
flat

nodes.name: Trivial bundle E^0 = M x M
nodes.statement:
Let $E^{0} \stackrel{{\rm def.}}{=}
M\times\mathcal{M}$ and let $\pi^0:M\times \mathcal{M}\rightarrow M$ and
$p^0:M\times\mathcal{M}\rightarrow \mathcal{M}$ denote the canonical
projections.
nodes.section: 2.2 Lorentzian Kaluza-Klein spaces

nodes.name: Vertical distribution of the trivial bundle
nodes.statement:
Let $V^0=(T\mathcal{M})^{p^0}$ denote the vertical
distribution of $\pi^0$, which is endowed with the pull-back metric
$\mathcal{G}^{p^0}$.
nodes.section: 2.2 Lorentzian Kaluza-Klein spaces

nodes.name: Topologically trivial Kaluza-Klein space
nodes.statement:
A {\em topologically trivial Kaluza-Klein space} over $(M,g)$ with
fiber $(\mathcal{M},\mathcal{G})$ is a Kaluza-Klein space of the form
$\pi^0:(E^0,h^{0})\rightarrow (M,g)$, whose vertical metric is the
pull-back metric $h_{V^0}\stackrel{{\rm def.}}{=} \mathcal{G}^{p^0}$.
nodes.section: 2.2 Lorentzian Kaluza-Klein spaces

nodes.name: Metric of a topologically trivial KK space
nodes.statement:
The metric $h^{0}=h(g,\mathcal{G},H)$ of such a space is uniquely determined by
$g$, $\mathcal{G}$ and by the horizontal distribution $H$, whose parallel
transport $T$ must preserve $\mathcal{G}^{p^0}$.
nodes.section: 2.2 Lorentzian Kaluza-Klein spaces

nodes.name: Reduced transport hat T
nodes.statement:
For any $\gamma\in \mathcal{P}(M)$
and all $p\in \mathcal{M}$, we define:
\begin{equation} T_\gamma(\gamma(0),p)=(\gamma(1),{\hat T}_\gamma(p))~~, 
\end{equation}
where ${\hat T}_\gamma\in \mathrm{Iso}(\mathcal{M},\mathcal{G})$ satisfy ${\hat T}_{\gamma_1\gamma_2}={\hat T}_{\gamma_1}\circ {\hat T}_{\gamma_2}$.
nodes.section: 2.2 Lorentzian Kaluza-Klein spaces

nodes.name: Reduced transport (hatT)
nodes.statement: T_\gamma(\gamma(0),p)=(\gamma(1),{\hat T}_\gamma(p))~~,
nodes.section: 2.2 Lorentzian Kaluza-Klein spaces
nodes.label: hatT

nodes.name: Product Kaluza-Klein space
nodes.statement:
The {\em product Kaluza-Klein space} over $(M,g)$ with fiber
$(\mathcal{M},\mathcal{G})$ is the topologically trivial Kaluza-Klein space
$\pi^0:(E^0,h^0_{\mathrm{triv}})\rightarrow (M,g)$ with fiber $(\mathcal{M},\mathcal{G})$
whose horizontal distribution is the trivial integrable Ehresmann
connection $H^0_{\mathrm{triv}} \stackrel{{\rm def.}}{=} (T M)^{\pi^0}$, with induced horizontal
metric $h^0_{\mathrm{triv}}$.
nodes.section: 2.2 Lorentzian Kaluza-Klein spaces

nodes.name: Proof that the trivial connection gives the product metric
nodes.statement:
For any $p\in \mathcal{M}$, the horizontal lift through $(\gamma(0),p)\in
E^0_{\gamma(0)}$ of any path $\gamma\in \mathcal{P}(M)$ defined by the
trivial Ehresmann connection $H^0$ is the path given by
$\boldsymbol{\gamma}_{p, \mathrm{triv}}(s)=(\gamma(s),p)$ for all $s\in [0,1]$. Hence the
Ehresmann transport $T^0_\gamma$ defined by $H^0$ is given by ${\hat
T}^0_{\gamma}=\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal{M}}$.
nodes.section: 2.2 Lorentzian Kaluza-Klein spaces
nodes.statement_short: Horizontal lifts of the trivial connection are constant in the fiber, so transport is the identity.

nodes.name: Product Kaluza-Klein metric
nodes.statement:
This implies that the Kaluza-Klein metric
$h^0_{\mathrm{triv}}=h_{g, \mathcal{G}, H^0_\mathrm{triv}}$ equals the product metric
$g\times \mathcal{G}$.
nodes.section: 2.2 Lorentzian Kaluza-Klein spaces
conclusions:
$h^0_{\mathrm{triv}}=h_{g, \mathcal{G}, H^0_\mathrm{triv}}$ equals the product metric
$g\times \mathcal{G}$

nodes.name: Classification of flat principal bundles by holonomy
nodes.statement:
It is well-known that flat
principal $G$-bundles are classified up to isomorphism by their
holonomy morphism $\mathrm{Hol}_{P,\theta}:\pi_1(M)\rightarrow G$, considered
up to the conjugation action of $G$.
nodes.section: 2.2 Lorentzian Kaluza-Klein spaces
conclusions:
flat
principal $G$-bundles are classified up to isomorphism by their
holonomy morphism $\mathrm{Hol}_{P,\theta}:\pi_1(M)\rightarrow G$, considered
up to the conjugation action of $G$

nodes.name: Integrable Kaluza-Klein spaces classified by a character variety
nodes.statement:
Hence the set of isomorphism
classes of integrable Kaluza-Klein spaces over $(M,g)$ with
fiber $(\mathcal{M},\mathcal{G})$ and Ehresmann holonomy contained in 
$\mathrm{Iso}(\mathcal{M},\mathcal{G})$ is in bijection with the character variety:
\begin{equation*}
\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{Iso}(\mathcal{M},\mathcal{G})}(M)\stackrel{{\rm def.}}{=} {\rm Hom}(\pi_1(M),\mathrm{Iso}(\mathcal{M},\mathcal{G}))/\mathrm{Iso}(\mathcal{M},\mathcal{G})\, .
\end{equation*}
nodes.section: 2.2 Lorentzian Kaluza-Klein spaces
nodes.statement_short: Integrable KK spaces with fiber (M,G) correspond to Hom(pi_1(M), Iso(M,G)) modulo conjugation.

nodes.name: Integrable KK spaces over simply-connected space-times are products
nodes.statement:
When the space-time $M$ is simply-connected, any integrable
Kaluza-Klein space over $(M,g)$ is isomorphic with a product space
(see below). In that case, we necessarily have $G=1$ (the trivial
group) and $H$ is gauge-equivalent with the trivial Ehresmann
connection.
nodes.section: 2.2 Lorentzian Kaluza-Klein spaces
conclusions:
any integrable
Kaluza-Klein space over $(M,g)$ is isomorphic with a product space

nodes.name: Vertical scalar potential
nodes.statement:
A \emph{vertical scalar potential} for $\pi$ is a smooth $T$-invariant
real-valued function $\mathbf{\Phi} \in \mathcal{C}^\infty(E,\mathbb{R})$ defined on the total
space $E$ of $\pi$.
nodes.section: 2.3 Vertical scalar potentials and scalar bundles

nodes.name: T-invariance equals horizontal annihilation
nodes.section: 2.3 Vertical scalar potentials and scalar bundles
nodes.statement_short: T-invariance of Phi is equivalent to X(Phi)=0 for all horizontal X.

nodes.name: Horizontal annihilation of the potential (Vvert)
nodes.statement: X(\mathbf{\Phi})=0\, , \quad \forall\, X\in \Gamma(E,H)\, .
nodes.section: 2.3 Vertical scalar potentials and scalar bundles
nodes.label: Vvert

nodes.name: Fiber restrictions of a vertical potential are recovered by transport
nodes.statement:
This implies that all fiber restrictions $\Phi_m$ ($m\in M$) can be
recovered from $\Phi_{m_0}$, where $m_0$ is any fixed point of $M$. In
particular, the isomorphism type of the scalar structure\footnote{As
defined in reference \cite{GESM}.} $(E_m,h_m,\Phi_m)$ is independent
of $m$.
nodes.section: 2.3 Vertical scalar potentials and scalar bundles

nodes.name: Holonomy preserves the potential
nodes.section: 2.3 Vertical scalar potentials and scalar bundles

nodes.name: Proof that dPhi is vertical
nodes.statement:
Relation \eqref{Vvert} amounts to $\mathrm{d} \mathbf{\Phi} (X)=0$ for all
$X\in\Gamma(X,H)$, i.e. $\mathrm{d} \mathbf{\Phi} \circ P_H=0$. Since
$P_V+P_H=\mathrm{id}_{TE}$, this gives $\mathrm{d} \mathbf{\Phi}=\mathrm{d} \mathbf{\Phi} \circ P_V$, which
shows that $\mathrm{d} \mathbf{\Phi}$ can be viewed as an element of
$\Gamma(E,V^\ast)$.
nodes.section: 2.3 Vertical scalar potentials and scalar bundles
nodes.statement_short: dPhi kills H, hence dPhi = dPhi o P_V.

nodes.name: Gradient of a vertical potential is vertical
nodes.section: 2.3 Vertical scalar potentials and scalar bundles
conclusions: the gradient of $\mathbf{\Phi}$ is a vertical vector field

nodes.name: Scalar bundle
nodes.statement:
A {\em scalar bundle} over $(M,g)$ is a pair $(\pi:(E,h)\rightarrow
(M,g),\mathbf{\Phi})$, where $\pi$ is a Kaluza-Klein space and $\mathbf{\Phi}$ is a
vertical scalar potential for $\pi$. The scalar bundle is called {\em
integrable} if the Kaluza-Klein space $\pi$ is integrable.
nodes.section: 2.3 Vertical scalar potentials and scalar bundles

nodes.name: Type of a scalar bundle
nodes.statement:
The isomorphism type of the scalar structures $(E_m,h_m,\Phi_m)$
(which, as explained above, does not depend on the point $m\in M$) is
called the {\em type} of the scalar bundle and will be generally
denoted by $(\mathcal{M},\mathcal{G},\Phi)$.
nodes.section: 2.3 Vertical scalar potentials and scalar bundles

nodes.name: Proof of classification of integrable scalar bundles
nodes.statement:
The classification of integrable
Kaluza-Klein spaces immediately implies the following.
nodes.section: 2.3 Vertical scalar potentials and scalar bundles
nodes.statement_short: Immediate from the classification of integrable Kaluza-Klein spaces.

nodes.name: Classification of integrable scalar bundles
nodes.section: 2.3 Vertical scalar potentials and scalar bundles
nodes.statement_short: Integrable scalar bundles of a given type correspond to points of the character variety of pi_1(M) in Iso(M,G,Phi).
assumptions:
Integrable scalar bundles defined over $(M,g)$ and having type
$(\mathcal{M},\mathcal{G},\Phi)$
conclusions:
are classified up to isomorphism by the points of the
character variety

nodes.name: Geodesically convex set
nodes.statement:
Recall that an open subset $U$ of a pseudo-Riemannian
manifold is called {\em geodesically convex} \cite{ONeillBook} if it
is a normal neighborhood for each of its points.
nodes.section: 2.4 Special trivializing atlases for a Kaluza-Klein space and for a scalar bundle
nodes.genus:
open subset $U$ of a pseudo-Riemannian
manifold
differentia:
it
is a normal neighborhood for each of its points

nodes.name: Unique geodesic segment in convex sets
nodes.statement:
If $U$ is convex,
then for any two points $p,q\in U$ there exists a unique geodesic
segment which is contained in $U$ and which connects $p$ and $q$.
nodes.section: 2.4 Special trivializing atlases for a Kaluza-Klein space and for a scalar bundle
conclusions:
for any two points $p,q\in U$ there exists a unique geodesic
segment which is contained in $U$ and which connects $p$ and $q$

nodes.name: Existence of convex neighborhoods
nodes.statement:
Any
point of a pseudo-Riemannian manifold has a basis of geodesically
convex neighborhoods (see \cite[p. 129]{ONeillBook}).
nodes.section: 2.4 Special trivializing atlases for a Kaluza-Klein space and for a scalar bundle

nodes.name: Convex cover
nodes.statement:
A {\em convex
  cover} of a pseudo-Riemannian manifold is an cover by open and
geodesically convex sets which has the property that any nontrivial
intersection of two of its elements is geodesically convex.
nodes.section: 2.4 Special trivializing atlases for a Kaluza-Klein space and for a scalar bundle

nodes.name: O'Neill Lemma 5.10 (refinement by convex covers)
nodes.statement:
Given
any open cover $\mathfrak{V}$ of a pseudo-Riemannian manifold, there
exists a convex cover $\mathfrak{U}$ such that any element of
$\mathfrak{U}$ is contained in some element of $\mathfrak{V}$
\cite[Lemma 5.10]{ONeillBook}.
nodes.section: 2.4 Special trivializing atlases for a Kaluza-Klein space and for a scalar bundle
assumptions:
Given
any open cover $\mathfrak{V}$ of a pseudo-Riemannian manifold
conclusions:
there
exists a convex cover $\mathfrak{U}$ such that any element of
$\mathfrak{U}$ is contained in some element of $\mathfrak{V}$

nodes.name: Pseudo-Riemannian manifolds admit convex covers
nodes.statement:
In particular, any pseudo-Riemannian 
manifold admits convex covers.
nodes.section: 2.4 Special trivializing atlases for a Kaluza-Klein space and for a scalar bundle

nodes.name: Convex cover (U_alpha)
nodes.statement:
Let $\mathfrak{U}=\left( U_\alpha\right)_{\alpha \in I}$ be
a convex cover for $(M,g)$, where the indexing set is chosen such that
$0\not \in I$.
nodes.section: 2.4 Special trivializing atlases for a Kaluza-Klein space and for a scalar bundle

nodes.name: Reference points and paths
nodes.statement:
Fix points $m_{\alpha}\in U_\alpha$ and paths
$\lambda^{\alpha}\in \mathcal{P}(M)$ such that
$\lambda^{\alpha}(0)=m_{\alpha}$ and $\lambda^{\alpha}(1)=m_0$.
nodes.section: 2.4 Special trivializing atlases for a Kaluza-Klein space and for a scalar bundle

nodes.name: Radial geodesics gamma_m^alpha
nodes.statement:
For
any $m\in U_\alpha$, let $\gamma_m^{\alpha}:[0,1]\rightarrow U_\alpha$
be the unique smooth geodesic contained in $U_\alpha$ such that
$\gamma_m^{\alpha}(0)=m$ and $\gamma_m^{\alpha}(1)=m_\alpha$.
nodes.section: 2.4 Special trivializing atlases for a Kaluza-Klein space and for a scalar bundle

nodes.name: Restrictions to U_alpha
nodes.section: 2.4 Special trivializing atlases for a Kaluza-Klein space and for a scalar bundle

nodes.name: Local trivial bundles E^0_alpha
nodes.statement:
Let
$E^0_{\alpha}\stackrel{{\rm def.}}{=} U_\alpha\times \mathcal{M}$ and $\pi^0_{\alpha}\colon
E_{\alpha}^{0}\rightarrow U_\alpha$, $p^0_{\alpha}\colon
E^0_{\alpha}\rightarrow \mathcal{M}$ be the projections on the first and
second factors.
nodes.section: 2.4 Special trivializing atlases for a Kaluza-Klein space and for a scalar bundle

nodes.name: Special trivializing maps q_alpha
nodes.statement:
Define diffeomorphisms
$q_\alpha:E_{\alpha}\rightarrow U_\alpha\times \mathcal{M}$ through:
\begin{equation} q_\alpha(e)=(\pi(e), {\hat q}_\alpha(e))\, , \quad  \forall\, e\in E_\alpha\, ,
\end{equation}
where ${\hat q}_\alpha\colon E_\alpha\rightarrow \mathcal{M}$ is given by the
following differentiable surjective map:
\begin{equation} \hat{q}_\alpha(e)\stackrel{{\rm def.}}{=} p^0_{\alpha}\circ (T_{\lambda^{\alpha}}\circ T_{\gamma^{\alpha}_{\pi(e)}})(e)=p^0_{\alpha}\circ T_{\lambda^{\alpha}\circ \gamma^{\alpha}_{\pi(e)}}(e)\in  \mathcal{M}\, , \qquad \forall\, e\in E_\alpha\, .
\end{equation}
nodes.section: 2.4 Special trivializing atlases for a Kaluza-Klein space and for a scalar bundle
nodes.statement_short: q_alpha transports each point along the geodesic to m_alpha and then along lambda^alpha to the reference fiber.

nodes.name: Trivializing map q_alpha (qalpha)
nodes.statement: q_\alpha(e)=(\pi(e), {\hat q}_\alpha(e))\, , \quad  \forall\, e\in E_\alpha\, ,
nodes.section: 2.4 Special trivializing atlases for a Kaluza-Klein space and for a scalar bundle
nodes.label: qalpha

nodes.name: Fiber component hat q_alpha (hatqalpha)
nodes.statement: \hat{q}_\alpha(e)\stackrel{{\rm def.}}{=} p^0_{\alpha}\circ (T_{\lambda^{\alpha}}\circ T_{\gamma^{\alpha}_{\pi(e)}})(e)=p^0_{\alpha}\circ T_{\lambda^{\alpha}\circ \gamma^{\alpha}_{\pi(e)}}(e)\in  \mathcal{M}\, , \qquad \forall\, e\in E_\alpha\, .
nodes.section: 2.4 Special trivializing atlases for a Kaluza-Klein space and for a scalar bundle
nodes.label: hatqalpha

nodes.name: Fiber restrictions of q_alpha are isometries
nodes.statement:
The restriction ${\hat q}_{\alpha}(m)\stackrel{{\rm def.}}{=} {\hat
  q}_\alpha|_{E_m}:E_m\rightarrow \mathcal{M}$ to the fiber at $m\in U_\alpha$
is an isometry from $(E_m,h_m)$ to $(\mathcal{M},\mathcal{G})$ which is given
explicitly by:
\begin{equation*}
{\hat q}_{\alpha}(m)(e_{m})=p^{0}_{\alpha}\circ T_{\lambda^{\alpha}\circ \gamma^{\alpha}_{m}}(m\times e_{m})\, , \quad \forall\, e_{m}\in E_m\, . 
\end{equation*}
nodes.section: 2.4 Special trivializing atlases for a Kaluza-Klein space and for a scalar bundle

nodes.name: Trivializing diagram
nodes.section: 2.4 Special trivializing atlases for a Kaluza-Klein space and for a scalar bundle

nodes.name: Trivializing diagram (ltriv)
nodes.section: 2.4 Special trivializing atlases for a Kaluza-Klein space and for a scalar bundle
nodes.label: ltriv

nodes.name: Special trivializing atlas
nodes.statement:
Hence $(U_\alpha, q_\alpha)$ is a trivializing atlas for the fiber
bundle $\pi$, called the {\em special trivializing atlas} determined
by the convex cover $(U_\alpha)_{\alpha\in I}$, by the reference
point $m_0$ and by the choices of points $m_{\alpha}\in U_\alpha$ and
of paths $\lambda^{\alpha}$ from $m_{\alpha}$ to $m_0$.
nodes.section: 2.4 Special trivializing atlases for a Kaluza-Klein space and for a scalar bundle

nodes.name: Restricted metric h_alpha
nodes.statement: Let $h_{\alpha}\stackrel{{\rm def.}}{=} h|_{E_{\alpha}}$.
nodes.section: 2.4 Special trivializing atlases for a Kaluza-Klein space and for a scalar bundle

nodes.name: Proof that q_alpha is a KK isomorphism
nodes.statement:
Since the Ehresmann transport
$T$ is isometric, the vertical metric $h_\alpha|_{V}$ agrees with
$\mathcal{G}^{p^0_{\alpha}}$ through the diffeomorphism $q_\alpha\colon
E_{\alpha}\rightarrow U_\alpha\times \mathcal{M}$. Hence $h_\alpha$
corresponds through $q_\alpha$ to a Kaluza-Klein metric
$h^{0}_{\alpha}$ on the trivial bundle
$\pi^0_{\alpha}:E_{\alpha}\rightarrow U_\alpha$.
nodes.section: 2.4 Special trivializing atlases for a Kaluza-Klein space and for a scalar bundle
nodes.statement_short: Isometric transport makes the vertical metric agree with the pulled-back fiber metric, so h_alpha transfers to a KK metric.

nodes.name: Local Kaluza-Klein metric h^0_alpha
nodes.statement:
The latter is the
Kaluza-Klein metric determined by $g|_{U_\alpha}$, $\mathcal{G}$ and the
distribution $H^{0}_{\alpha} \stackrel{{\rm def.}}{=} (\mathrm{d} q_\alpha)(H_\alpha)$, where
$H_\alpha\stackrel{{\rm def.}}{=} H|_{E_\alpha}$.
nodes.section: 2.4 Special trivializing atlases for a Kaluza-Klein space and for a scalar bundle

nodes.name: q_alpha is an isomorphism of Kaluza-Klein spaces
nodes.statement:
The diffeomorphism $q_\alpha$ is an
isometry from $(E_\alpha,h_\alpha)$ to $(E^0_{\alpha},
h^{0}_{\alpha})$ which makes diagram \eqref{ltriv} into an isomorphism
of Kaluza-Klein spaces from the Kaluza-Klein space
$\pi_\alpha:(E_\alpha,h_\alpha)\rightarrow (U_\alpha,g_\alpha)$ to the
Kaluza-Klein space $\pi^0_{\alpha}\colon
(E^0_{\alpha},h^{0}_{\alpha})\rightarrow (U_\alpha,g_\alpha)$.
nodes.section: 2.4 Special trivializing atlases for a Kaluza-Klein space and for a scalar bundle

nodes.name: Kaluza-Klein spaces are locally topologically trivial
nodes.statement:
Since $(M,g)$ admits convex covers, any Kaluza-Klein space admits
special trivializing atlases. In particular, any Kaluza-Klein space is
locally isomorphic with a topologically trivial Kaluza-Klein space
(which need not be a product Kaluza-Klein space!).
nodes.section: 2.4 Special trivializing atlases for a Kaluza-Klein space and for a scalar bundle

nodes.name: Transition functions of a special trivializing atlas
nodes.section: 2.4 Special trivializing atlases for a Kaluza-Klein space and for a scalar bundle

nodes.name: Transition functions (bgdef)
nodes.statement: \mathbf{g}_{\alpha\beta}(m)\stackrel{{\rm def.}}{=} {\hat q}_\beta(m)\circ {\hat q}^{-1}_\alpha(m)\in \mathrm{Iso}(\mathcal{M},\mathcal{G})\, , \quad \forall\, m\in U_{\alpha\beta}\, .
nodes.section: 2.4 Special trivializing atlases for a Kaluza-Klein space and for a scalar bundle
nodes.label: bgdef

nodes.name: Transition functions are transports along closed loops
nodes.section: 2.4 Special trivializing atlases for a Kaluza-Klein space and for a scalar bundle

nodes.name: Closed path c^{alpha beta}_m
nodes.statement:
Here: 
\begin{equation} c^{\alpha\beta}_m\stackrel{{\rm def.}}{=}
\lambda^{\beta}\circ\gamma^{\beta}_{m}\circ (\gamma^{\alpha}_{m})^{-1}\circ (\lambda^{\alpha})^{-1}\, ,
\end{equation} 
is the closed path starting and ending at $m_0$ and passing through the
point $m\in U_{\alpha\beta}$ which is shown in
Figure \ref{fig:specialtriv}.
nodes.section: 2.4 Special trivializing atlases for a Kaluza-Klein space and for a scalar bundle

nodes.name: Closed path c^{alpha beta}_m (calphabeta)
nodes.statement:
c^{\alpha\beta}_m\stackrel{{\rm def.}}{=}
\lambda^{\beta}\circ\gamma^{\beta}_{m}\circ (\gamma^{\alpha}_{m})^{-1}\circ (\lambda^{\alpha})^{-1}\, ,
nodes.section: 2.4 Special trivializing atlases for a Kaluza-Klein space and for a scalar bundle
nodes.label: calphabeta

nodes.name: Special trivializing atlas for a scalar bundle
nodes.statement:
Let $\mathbf{\Phi}$ be a vertical potential for $\pi$. In this case, a
special trivializing atlas for the Kaluza-Klein space $\pi$ is also
called a special trivializing atlas for the scalar bundle
$(\pi,\mathbf{\Phi})$.
nodes.section: 2.4 Special trivializing atlases for a Kaluza-Klein space and for a scalar bundle
nodes.definiendum: special trivializing atlas for the scalar bundle

nodes.name: Local potentials Phi_alpha
nodes.statement:
Let $\mathbf{\Phi}_{\alpha} \stackrel{{\rm def.}}{=} \mathbf{\Phi}|_{E_\alpha}$ and set
$\Phi\stackrel{{\rm def.}}{=} \Phi_{m_0}$.
nodes.section: 2.4 Special trivializing atlases for a Kaluza-Klein space and for a scalar bundle

nodes.name: Local form of the vertical potential
nodes.statement:
Since $\mathbf{\Phi}$ is $T$-invariant, the
definition \eqref{hatqalpha} of ${\hat q}_\alpha$ implies:
\begin{equation} \mathbf{\Phi}_\alpha=\Phi\circ {\hat q}_\alpha\, .
\end{equation}
nodes.section: 2.4 Special trivializing atlases for a Kaluza-Klein space and for a scalar bundle

nodes.name: Local potential (bPhialpha)
nodes.statement: \mathbf{\Phi}_\alpha=\Phi\circ {\hat q}_\alpha\, .
nodes.section: 2.4 Special trivializing atlases for a Kaluza-Klein space and for a scalar bundle
nodes.label: bPhialpha

nodes.name: Transition functions preserve Phi
nodes.statement:
This gives $\Phi\circ \mathbf{g}_{\alpha\beta}=\Phi$,
i.e. $\mathbf{g}_{\alpha\beta}\in \mathrm{Iso}(\mathcal{M},\mathcal{G},\Phi)$.
nodes.section: 2.4 Special trivializing atlases for a Kaluza-Klein space and for a scalar bundle

nodes.name: Proof of local triviality in the integrable case
nodes.statement:
When the Kaluza-Klein space $\pi$ is integrable, the Ehresmann
transport depends only on the homotopy class of curves in $M$.  In
this case, $T_{c^{\alpha\beta}_m}$ is independent of the point $m\in
U_\alpha\cap U_\beta$ since $U_\alpha\cap U_\beta$ is path connected
and hence the homotopy class of $c^{\alpha\beta}_m$ does not depend on
$m$. Moreover, integrability of $H$ implies that $H_{\alpha}^{0}$
coincide with the trivial Ehresmann connections $H_{\alpha}^{\mathrm{triv}}$
of $\pi^0_{\alpha}$.  In this case, $\pi^0_{\alpha}\colon
(E^0_{\alpha}, h_\alpha)\rightarrow (U_\alpha,g_\alpha)$ is a product
Kaluza-Klein space and $q_\alpha$ is an isometry from $(E_{\alpha},
h_\alpha)$ to $(U_\alpha\times\mathcal{M},g_\alpha\times \mathcal{G})$. Thus:
nodes.section: 2.4 Special trivializing atlases for a Kaluza-Klein space and for a scalar bundle
nodes.statement_short: Integrability makes transport homotopy-invariant, so transition functions are constant and local connections trivial.

nodes.name: Special trivializing atlases of integrable Kaluza-Klein spaces
nodes.statement:
Let $\pi:(E,h)\rightarrow (M,g)$ be an integrable Kaluza-Klein
space. Then the local trivializing maps $q_\alpha$ of a special
trivializing atlas consist on isometries from $(E_{\alpha}, h_\alpha)$
to $(U_\alpha\times \mathcal{M},g_\alpha\times\mathcal{G})$ and the transition
functions $\mathbf{g}_{\alpha\beta}$ defined by such an atlas are constant on
$U_\alpha\cap U_\beta$. In particular, $\pi$ is locally isomorphic
with a product Kaluza-Klein space.
nodes.section: 2.4 Special trivializing atlases for a Kaluza-Klein space and for a scalar bundle
nodes.statement_short: For integrable KK spaces, special trivializing maps are isometries onto products and transition functions are locally constant.

nodes.name: Constant transition functions preserve the potential
nodes.statement:
Suppose that the integrable Kaluza-Klein space $\pi$ is endowed with a
vertical potential $\mathbf{\Phi}$ whose restriction to $\mathcal{M}$ we denote by
$\Phi$. Then the constant transition functions in a special
trivializing atlas satisfy $\mathbf{g}_{\alpha\beta}\in \mathrm{Iso}(\mathcal{M},\mathcal{G},\Phi)$.

$P_V:TE\rightarrow V$ and $P_H:TE\rightarrow H$ denote the
corresponding $h$-orthogonal projectors and $T$ denote the Ehresmann

nodes.name: Section sigma model
nodes.statement:
The {\em section sigma model} defined by $\pi$ and $\mathbf{\Phi}$ has action
functional $S_{\mathrm{sc}}\colon\mathrm{Met}_{3+n,1}(E)\times \Gamma(\pi)\rightarrow
\mathbb{R}$ given by:
\begin{equation} S_{\mathrm{sc},U}[g, h, s]=-\int_U\nu_M(g)e^v_\mathbf{\Phi}(g,h,s)
\end{equation}
for any relatively-compact subset $U\subset M$.
nodes.section: 3.1 The scalar section sigma model defined by $\pi$ and $\mathbf{\Phi}$
nodes.statement_short: Action S = -integral of the vertical Lagrange density over sections of the Kaluza-Klein space.

nodes.name: Section sigma model action (Ssc)
nodes.statement: S_{\mathrm{sc},U}[g, h, s]=-\int_U\nu_M(g)e^v_\mathbf{\Phi}(g,h,s)
nodes.section: 3.1 The scalar section sigma model defined by $\pi$ and $\mathbf{\Phi}$
nodes.label: Ssc

nodes.name: Vertical tension field
nodes.statement:
The {\em vertical tension field} of $s\in \Gamma(\pi)$ is defined
through:
\begin{equation*} \tau^v(g, h, s)\stackrel{{\rm def.}}{=} \mathrm{Tr}_{g}\nabla^v \mathrm{d}^v s \in \Gamma(M,V^s)~~.
\end{equation*}
nodes.section: 3.1 The scalar section sigma model defined by $\pi$ and $\mathbf{\Phi}$

nodes.name: Vertical tension field (tensionvert)
nodes.statement: \tau^v(g, h, s)\stackrel{{\rm def.}}{=} \mathrm{Tr}_{g}\nabla^v \mathrm{d}^v s \in \Gamma(M,V^s)~~.
nodes.section: 3.1 The scalar section sigma model defined by $\pi$ and $\mathbf{\Phi}$
nodes.label: tensionvert

nodes.name: Ordinary Lagrange density and tension field of a section
nodes.statement:
The ordinary Lagrange density and tension field of $s\in\Gamma(\pi)$
are defined similarly to their vertical counterparts except that there
is no vertical projection involved. More precisely, we define:
\begin{equation*}
e_\mathbf{\Phi}(g,h,s)\stackrel{{\rm def.}}{=} \frac{1}{2}\mathrm{Tr}_{g} s^\ast (h)+\mathbf{\Phi}^s\, ,
\end{equation*}
as well as:
\begin{equation*}
\tau(g, h, s)\stackrel{{\rm def.}}{=} \mathrm{Tr}_{g}\nabla \mathrm{d} s \in \Gamma(M,TE^s)\, ,
\end{equation*}
where $\nabla$ denotes the connection on $T^{\ast}M\otimes TE^{s}$
induced by the Levi-Civita connection on $(M,g)$ and the $s$-pullback
of the Levi-Civita connection on $(E,h)$. For simplicity we will
sometimes drop the explicit dependence on $g$ and $h$ in
$e_{\mathbf{\Phi}}(g,h,s)$, $\tau(g, h, s)$ etc.
nodes.section: 3.1 The scalar section sigma model defined by $\pi$ and $\mathbf{\Phi}$

nodes.name: Equations of motion of the section sigma model
nodes.statement:
The vertical density $e^v(s)$ differs from $e(s)$ by a constant and we
have $\tau^v(s)=P_V\circ\tau(s)$. Moreover, the critical points
of \eqref{Ssc} with respect to $s\in \Gamma(\pi)$ are solutions of the
equation:
\begin{equation} \tau^v(s)=-(\mathrm{grad}_h\mathbf{\Phi})^s\, .
\end{equation}
nodes.section: 3.1 The scalar section sigma model defined by $\pi$ and $\mathbf{\Phi}$

conclusions: The vertical density $e^v(s)$ differs from $e(s)$ by a constant
$\tau^v(s)=P_V\circ\tau(s)$

nodes.name: Section sigma model equation of motion (sceom)
nodes.statement: \tau^v(s)=-(\mathrm{grad}_h\mathbf{\Phi})^s\, .
nodes.section: 3.1 The scalar section sigma model defined by $\pi$ and $\mathbf{\Phi}$
nodes.label: sceom

nodes.name: Pseudoharmonic section
nodes.statement:
When $\mathbf{\Phi}=0$, equation \eqref{sceom} becomes the {\em vertical
pseudoharmonic equation}:
\begin{equation*} \tau^v(s)=0
\end{equation*}
and its solutions are called {\em pseudoharmonic sections} of $\pi$.
nodes.section: 3.1 The scalar section sigma model defined by $\pi$ and $\mathbf{\Phi}$

nodes.name: Vertical pseudoharmonic equation (pseudoharm)
nodes.statement: \tau^v(s)=0
nodes.section: 3.1 The scalar section sigma model defined by $\pi$ and $\mathbf{\Phi}$
nodes.label: pseudoharm

nodes.name: Argument: only vertical variations
nodes.statement:
Notice that \eqref{Ssc} is extremized only with respect to vertical
variations of $s$, since $s$ is subject to the section constraint
$\pi\circ s=\mathrm{id}_M$.
nodes.section: 3.1 The scalar section sigma model defined by $\pi$ and $\mathbf{\Phi}$
nodes.statement_short: The section constraint allows only vertical variations.

nodes.name: Pseudo-harmonic maps vs pseudo-harmonic sections
nodes.statement:
As a consequence, a section which is
pseudo-harmonic as an unconstrained map from $(M,g)$ to $(E,h)$ is a
pseudo-harmonic section, but not every pseudo-harmonic section is
pseudo-harmonic as an unconstrained map from $(M,g)$ to $(E,h)$.
nodes.section: 3.1 The scalar section sigma model defined by $\pi$ and $\mathbf{\Phi}$

nodes.name: Sheaf of configurations
nodes.statement:
The sheaf of configurations $\mathrm{Conf}_\pi$, which coincides with
  the sheaf of local smooth sections of $\pi$.
nodes.section: 3.2 The sheaves of configurations and solutions

nodes.name: Sheaf of solutions of the section sigma model
nodes.statement:
The sheaf of solutions $\mathrm{Sol}_{\pi,\Phi}$, defined as the
  sub-sheaf of $\mathrm{Conf}_\pi$ whose set of sections $\mathrm{Sol}_{\pi,\Phi}(U)$
  over an open subset $U\subset M$ consist of pseudo-harmonic sections
  of the restricted Kaluza-Klein space $\pi_U:(E_U,h_U)\rightarrow
  (U,g_U)$ endowed with the vertical potential $\Phi|_{E_U}$, where
  $E_U\stackrel{{\rm def.}}{=} \pi^{-1}(U)$, $h_U\stackrel{{\rm def.}}{=} h|_{E_U}$, $\pi_U\stackrel{{\rm def.}}{=}
  \pi|_{E_U}$ and $g_U\stackrel{{\rm def.}}{=} g|_{U}$.
nodes.section: 3.2 The sheaves of configurations and solutions

nodes.name: graph and ungraph maps
nodes.section: 3.3 A modified sigma model for maps

nodes.name: Modified scalar sigma model
nodes.statement:
The {\em modified scalar sigma model} determined by $(M,g)$,
$(\mathcal{M},\mathcal{G})$ and $H^0$ is defined by the action:
\begin{equation*}
S^{H^0}_{\mathrm{sc},\mathbf{\Phi}, U^0}[\varphi]=S_{\mathrm{sc},\pi^0, \mathbf{\Phi}, U^0}[\mathrm{graph}(\varphi)]\, .
\end{equation*}
for any relatively compact open set $U^0\subset M$, where
$S_{\mathrm{sc}, \pi, \mathbf{\Phi}, U^0}$ is the action of the section sigma model of
the topologically trivial Kaluza-Klein space $\pi^0\colon
(E^0,h^0)\rightarrow (M,g)$ with fiber $(\mathcal{M},\mathcal{G})$ and horizontal
distribution $H^0$.
nodes.section: 3.3 A modified sigma model for maps

nodes.name: H^0-pseudoharmonic map
nodes.statement:
Let $H^0$ be any horizontal distribution for the trivial bundle
$\pi^0\colon E^0\rightarrow M$.  A map $\varphi:(M,g)\rightarrow
(\mathcal{M},\mathcal{G})$ is called {\em $H^0$-pseudoharmonic} if the graph $s^0$ of
$\varphi$ is a pseudo-harmonic section of the topologically trivial
Kaluza-Klein space $\pi^0\colon (E^0,h^{0})\rightarrow (M,g)$ with
fiber $(\mathcal{M},\mathcal{G})$, where $h^{0}$ is the metric on $E^{0}$ determined
by $H^{0}, \mathcal{G}$ and $g$.
nodes.section: 3.3 A modified sigma model for maps

nodes.name: Solutions of the modified sigma model are H^0-pseudoharmonic
nodes.statement:
It is clear that the solutions of the equations of motion of the
modified scalar sigma model are $H^0$-pseudoharmonic maps.
nodes.section: 3.3 A modified sigma model for maps

nodes.name: Product Kaluza-Klein space reduces to the ordinary sigma model
nodes.statement:
Let $\pi^0:(E^0\stackrel{{\rm def.}}{=} M\times\mathcal{M}, h^0\stackrel{{\rm def.}}{=} g\times \mathcal{G})\rightarrow
(M,g)$ be the product Kaluza-Klein space with fiber $(\mathcal{M},\mathcal{G})$
defined over $(M,g)$ and horizontal distribution $H^{0}_{\mathrm{triv}}$. For
any $s\in \Gamma(\pi^0)$, we have $s^\ast(h)=\varphi^\ast (\mathcal{G})$ and
$\mathrm{d}^v s=\mathrm{d} \varphi$, where $\varphi=\mathrm{ungraph}(s)=p^0\circ s$. Thus
$e^v(s)=e(\varphi)$ and $\tau^v(s)=\tau(\varphi)$. Moreover, we have
$\mathbf{\Phi}=\Phi\circ p^0$ for some $\Phi\in \mathcal{C}^\infty(\mathcal{M},\mathbb{R})$. Hence the
section sigma model action \eqref{Ssc} reduces to the action of an
ordinary sigma model of maps from $(M,g)$ to $(\mathcal{M},\mathcal{G})$, while the
equations of motion \eqref{sceom} reduce to those of an ordinary sigma
model. Setting $\Phi=0$, we conclude that a map
$\varphi:(M,g)\rightarrow (\mathcal{M},\mathcal{G})$ is $H^0_\mathrm{triv}$-pseudoharmonic if
and only if it is pseudo-harmonic.
nodes.section: 3.3 A modified sigma model for maps
nodes.statement_short: For the product KK space the section sigma model is the ordinary sigma model; H^0_triv-pseudoharmonic equals pseudo-harmonic.

nodes.name: Form of q_{alpha beta} in the integrable case
nodes.statement:
For any pair of indices $\alpha,\beta\in I$ such
that $U_{\alpha\beta}\stackrel{{\rm def.}}{=} U_\alpha\cap U_\beta$ is non-empty, the
composition $q_{\alpha\beta}\stackrel{{\rm def.}}{=} q_\beta\circ
q_\alpha^{-1}:U_{\alpha\beta}\times \mathcal{M}\rightarrow
U_{\alpha\beta}\times \mathcal{M}$ has the form
$q_{\alpha\beta}(m,p)=(m,\mathbf{g}_{\alpha\beta}(p))$, where:
\begin{equation*}
\mathbf{g}_{\alpha\beta}\in \mathrm{Iso}(\mathcal{M},\mathcal{G},\Phi)\, .
\end{equation*}
nodes.section: 3.4 U-fold interpretation of globally-defined solutions in the integrable case

nodes.name: Cocycle condition for constant transition functions
nodes.statement:
Setting
$\mathbf{g}_{\alpha\beta}=\mathrm{id}_\mathcal{M}$ for $U_{\alpha\beta}=\emptyset$, the
collection $(\mathbf{g}_{\alpha\beta})_{\alpha,\beta\in I}$ satisfies the
cocycle condition:
\begin{equation} \mathbf{g}_{\beta\delta}\mathbf{g}_{\alpha\beta}=\mathbf{g}_{\alpha\delta}\, , \quad \forall\, \alpha,\beta,\delta\in I\, .
\end{equation}
nodes.section: 3.4 U-fold interpretation of globally-defined solutions in the integrable case

nodes.name: Cocycle condition (gcocycle)
nodes.statement: \mathbf{g}_{\beta\delta}\mathbf{g}_{\alpha\beta}=\mathbf{g}_{\alpha\delta}\, , \quad \forall\, \alpha,\beta,\delta\in I\, .
nodes.section: 3.4 U-fold interpretation of globally-defined solutions in the integrable case
nodes.label: gcocycle

nodes.name: Local maps phi^alpha of a section
nodes.statement:
For any section $s\in \Gamma(\pi)$, the restriction $s_\alpha\stackrel{{\rm def.}}{=}
s|_{U_\alpha}$ corresponds through $q_\alpha$ to the graph
$\mathrm{graph}(\varphi^{\alpha})\in \Gamma(\pi^0_{\alpha})$ of a
uniquely-defined smooth map
$\varphi^{\alpha}\in\mathcal{C}^\infty(U_\alpha,\mathcal{M})$:
\begin{equation} s_\alpha=q_{\alpha}^{-1}\circ \mathrm{graph}(\varphi^\alpha)~~\mathrm{i.e.}~~q_\alpha(s_\alpha(m))=(m,\varphi^\alpha(m))\, , ~~\forall m\in U_\alpha\, .
\end{equation}
nodes.section: 3.4 U-fold interpretation of globally-defined solutions in the integrable case

nodes.name: Local maps of a section (sres)
nodes.statement: s_\alpha=q_{\alpha}^{-1}\circ \mathrm{graph}(\varphi^\alpha)~~\mathrm{i.e.}~~q_\alpha(s_\alpha(m))=(m,\varphi^\alpha(m))\, , ~~\forall m\in U_\alpha\, .
nodes.section: 3.4 U-fold interpretation of globally-defined solutions in the integrable case
nodes.label: sres

nodes.section: 3.4 U-fold interpretation of globally-defined solutions in the integrable case

nodes.name: Gluing condition for local maps
nodes.statement:
Using relation \eqref{bgflat}, this implies:
\begin{equation} \varphi^{\beta}(m)=\mathbf{g}_{\alpha\beta}\varphi^{\alpha}(m)~~\forall m\in U_{\alpha\beta}~~,
\end{equation}
where juxtaposition in the right hand side denotes the tautological
action of the group $\mathrm{Iso}(\mathcal{M},\mathcal{G},\Phi)$ on $\mathcal{M}$.
nodes.section: 3.4 U-fold interpretation of globally-defined solutions in the integrable case

nodes.name: Gluing of local maps (phigluing)
nodes.statement: \varphi^{\beta}(m)=\mathbf{g}_{\alpha\beta}\varphi^{\alpha}(m)~~\forall m\in U_{\alpha\beta}~~,
nodes.section: 3.4 U-fold interpretation of globally-defined solutions in the integrable case
nodes.label: phigluing

nodes.name: Local maps satisfying the gluing condition define a section
nodes.statement:
Conversely, any
family of smooth maps
$\left\{\varphi^{\alpha}\in\mathcal{C}^\infty(U_\alpha,\mathcal{M})\right\}_{\alpha\in
I}$ satisfying \eqref{phigluing} defines a smooth section
$s\in \Gamma(\pi)$ whose restrictions to $U_\alpha$ are given
by \eqref{sres}.
nodes.section: 3.4 U-fold interpretation of globally-defined solutions in the integrable case

nodes.name: Local equivalence of equations of motion (integrable case)
nodes.statement:
From the previous discussion, the equation of motion \eqref{sceom} for
$s$ is equivalent with the condition that each $\varphi^{\alpha}$
satisfies the equation of motion of the ordinary sigma model defined
by the scalar data $(\mathcal{M},\mathcal{G},\Phi)$ on the space-time
$(U_\alpha,g_\alpha)$:
\begin{equation} \tau^v(h, s)=-(\mathrm{grad} \mathbf{\Phi})^s \Leftrightarrow \tau(g_\alpha, \varphi^{\alpha})=-(\mathrm{grad}\Phi)^{\varphi^{\alpha}} ~~\forall \alpha\in I~~.
\end{equation}
nodes.section: 3.4 U-fold interpretation of globally-defined solutions in the integrable case
nodes.statement_short: The section sigma model equation is equivalent to the ordinary sigma model equation for each local map.

nodes.name: Local equations of motion (localeomscalar)
nodes.statement: \tau^v(h, s)=-(\mathrm{grad} \mathbf{\Phi})^s \Leftrightarrow \tau(g_\alpha, \varphi^{\alpha})=-(\mathrm{grad}\Phi)^{\varphi^{\alpha}} ~~\forall \alpha\in I~~.
nodes.section: 3.4 U-fold interpretation of globally-defined solutions in the integrable case
nodes.label: localeomscalar

nodes.name: Global solutions glued from local sigma-model solutions
nodes.statement:
Thus global solutions $s$ of the equations of motion \eqref{sceom} are
\emph{glued} from local solutions $\varphi^{\alpha}\in
\mathcal{C}^\infty(U_\alpha,\mathcal{M})$ of the equations of motion of the ordinary
sigma model using the $\mathrm{Iso}(\mathcal{M},\mathcal{G},\Phi)$-valued constant transition
functions $\mathbf{g}_{\alpha\beta}$ which satisfy the cocycle condition
\eqref{gcocycle}.
nodes.section: 3.4 U-fold interpretation of globally-defined solutions in the integrable case

nodes.section: 3.5 Sheaf-theoretical description

nodes.name: Sheaf isomorphisms preserve solutions
nodes.statement:
Since $\mathbf{g}_{\alpha\beta}$ acts by symmetries of the equations of
motion of the ordinary sigma model, this restricts to an isomorphism
of sheaves of sets from
$\mathrm{Sol}^{g,{\alpha}}_{\mathcal{M},\mathcal{G},\Phi}|_{U_{\alpha\beta}}$ to
$\mathrm{Sol}^{g,\beta}_{\mathcal{M},\mathcal{G},\Phi}|_{U_{\alpha\beta}}$.
nodes.section: 3.5 Sheaf-theoretical description

nodes.name: Cocycle condition for sheaf isomorphisms
nodes.section: 3.5 Sheaf-theoretical description

nodes.name: Glued sheaves Conf_M and Sol_M
nodes.statement:
The sheaves $\mathrm{Conf}_\mathcal{M}^{\alpha}$ and $\mathrm{Sol}_{\mathcal{M},\mathcal{G},\Phi}^{g,\alpha}$
defined on $U_\alpha$ glue using these isomorphisms to sheaves
$\mathbf{Conf}_\mathcal{M}$ and $\mathbf{Sol}^{g}_{\mathcal{M},\mathcal{G},\Phi}\subset \mathbf{Conf}_\mathcal{M}$ defined
on $M$ which satisfy $\mathbf{Conf}_\mathcal{M}|_{U_\alpha}\simeq \mathrm{Conf}_\mathcal{M}^{\alpha}$
and
$\mathbf{Sol}_{\mathcal{M},\mathcal{G},\Phi}^{g}|_{U_\alpha}\simeq \mathrm{Sol}_{\mathcal{M},\mathcal{G},\Phi}^{g,\alpha}$.
nodes.section: 3.5 Sheaf-theoretical description

nodes.name: Sheaf-theoretic U-fold interpretation
nodes.statement:
The
discussion above shows that the trivialization maps $q_\alpha$ of
$\pi$ induce isomorphisms of sheaves:
\begin{equation*}
\mathrm{Conf}_\pi\simeq \mathbf{Conf}_\mathcal{M}\, , \quad \mathrm{Sol}_{\pi,\mathbf{\Phi}}\simeq \mathbf{Sol}_{\mathcal{M},\mathcal{G},\Phi}^{g}\, .
\end{equation*}
which present $\mathbf{Conf}_\mathcal{M}$ and $\mathbf{Sol}_{\mathcal{M},\mathcal{G},\Phi}$ respectively as
the sheaves of configurations and solutions of the section sigma model
defined by the scalar structure $(\pi,\mathbf{\Phi})$.
nodes.section: 3.5 Sheaf-theoretical description
nodes.statement_short: q_alpha induce isomorphisms Conf_pi = Conf_M and Sol_pi = Sol_M of sheaves.

nodes.name: Classical scalar locally-geometric U-fold
nodes.statement:
A {\em classical scalar locally-geometric U-fold} of type
$(\mathcal{M},\mathcal{G},\Phi)$ is a smooth global solution $s\in \Gamma(\pi)$ of the
equations of motion \eqref{sceom} of the section sigma model defined
by an {\em integrable} bundle of scalar data ($\pi:(E,h)\rightarrow
(M,g),\mathbf{\Phi})$ having type $(\mathcal{M},\mathcal{G},\Phi)$.
nodes.section: 3.6 Classical scalar locally-geometric U-folds

nodes.name: U-folds are glued from local sigma-model solutions
nodes.statement:
As explained above, any such object can be constructed by gluing local
solutions of the ordinary sigma model with target $(\mathcal{M},\mathcal{G})$ using
the $\mathrm{Iso}(\mathcal{M},\mathcal{G},\Phi)$-valued transition functions of
$\pi$.
nodes.section: 3.6 Classical scalar locally-geometric U-folds

nodes.name: Integrable section sigma models are locally ordinary sigma models
nodes.statement:
Moreover, the discussion above shows that a section sigma model
based on an integrable Kaluza-Klein space is {\em locally
indistinguishable} from an ordinary sigma model.
nodes.section: 3.6 Classical scalar locally-geometric U-folds

nodes.name: Continuum of inequivalent global formulations
nodes.statement:
When the space-time $M$ is not simply-connected, the
number of inequivalent global formulations of this type is in general
{\em continuously infinite}, since so is the character variety of
$\pi_1(M)$ for the group $\mathrm{Iso}(\mathcal{M},\mathcal{G},\Phi)$.
nodes.section: 3.6 Classical scalar locally-geometric U-folds

nodes.name: Fiber restrictions of the symplectic bundle
nodes.statement:
Given a point $m\in M$, let
$(\mathcal{S}_m,D_m,\omega_m)$ be the restriction of $(\boldsymbol{\mathcal{S}},\boldsymbol{\omega},\mathbf{D})$ to
the fiber $E_m$.
nodes.section: 4 Scalar-electromagnetic bundles

nodes.name: Fiber restrictions are duality structures
nodes.statement:
This is a flat symplectic vector bundle defined on
the Riemannian manifold $(E_m,h_m)$ and hence a duality structure as
defined in \cite{GESM}.
nodes.section: 4 Scalar-electromagnetic bundles

nodes.name: Parallel transport U_Gamma
nodes.statement:
For any path $\Gamma\in\mathcal{P}(E)$ in the total
space of $E$, let $U_\Gamma:\boldsymbol{\mathcal{S}}_{\Gamma(0)}\rightarrow
\boldsymbol{\mathcal{S}}_{\Gamma(1)}$ be the parallel transport defined by $\mathbf{D}$ along
$\Gamma$.
nodes.section: 4 Scalar-electromagnetic bundles

nodes.name: Symplectic parallel transport is a symplectomorphism
nodes.statement:
Since $\mathbf{D}$ is a symplectic connection, $U_\Gamma$ is a
symplectomorphism between the symplectic vector spaces
$(\boldsymbol{\mathcal{S}}_{\Gamma(0)}, \boldsymbol{\omega}_{\Gamma(0)})$ and
$(\boldsymbol{\mathcal{S}}_{\Gamma(1)},\boldsymbol{\omega}_{\Gamma(1)})$.
nodes.section: 4 Scalar-electromagnetic bundles

nodes.name: Horizontal lift of a path
nodes.statement:
For any path $\gamma\in
\mathcal{P}(M)$, let $\boldsymbol{\gamma}_e\in \mathcal{P}(E)$ denote its horizontal lift starting
at the point $e\in E_{\gamma(0)}$.
nodes.section: 4 Scalar-electromagnetic bundles

nodes.name: Extended horizontal transport
nodes.statement:
The {\em extended horizontal transport} along a path
$\gamma\in \mathcal{P}(M)$ is the unbased isomorphism of vector bundles
$\mathbf{T}_\gamma:\mathcal{S}_{\gamma(0)}\rightarrow \mathcal{S}_{\gamma(1)}$ defined
through:
\begin{equation*}
\mathbf{T}_\gamma(e)\stackrel{{\rm def.}}{=} U_{\boldsymbol{\gamma}_e}:\mathcal{S}_{e}\rightarrow \mathcal{S}_{T_\gamma(e)}\, , \quad \forall\, e\in E_{\gamma(0)}\, ,
\end{equation*}
which linearizes the Ehresmann transport $T_\gamma:E_{\gamma(0)}\rightarrow E_{\gamma(1)}$ along $\gamma$.
nodes.section: 4 Scalar-electromagnetic bundles

nodes.name: Extended transport is an isomorphism of flat symplectic bundles
nodes.section: 4 Scalar-electromagnetic bundles

nodes.name: Duality bundle
nodes.statement:
Let $\pi\colon (E,h)\to (M,g)$ be a Kaluza-Klein space. A
\emph{duality bundle} $\boldsymbol{\Delta}$ is a flat symplectic vector bundle
$\boldsymbol{\Delta} = (\boldsymbol{\mathcal{S}},\boldsymbol{\omega},\mathbf{D})$ over $E$. Let $\boldsymbol{\Delta}_{1}$ and
$\boldsymbol{\Delta}_{2}$ be duality bundles. A \emph{morphism of duality bundles}
from $\boldsymbol{\Delta}_{1}$ to $\boldsymbol{\Delta}_{2}$ is a bundle morphism of the
underlying flat symplectic vector bundles.
nodes.section: 4 Scalar-electromagnetic bundles

nodes.name: Duality bundle recovered from one fiber
nodes.statement:
Since $M$ is
path-connected, it follows that all fiber restrictions
$(\mathcal{S}_m,D_m,\omega_m)$, $m\in M$, can be recovered by extended
horizontal transport from the flat symplectic vector bundle
$(\mathcal{S}_{m_0},D_{m_0},\omega_{m_0})$ over $E_{m_0}$.
nodes.section: 4 Scalar-electromagnetic bundles

nodes.name: Type of a duality bundle
nodes.statement:
In particular, the isomorphism class of the duality
structures $\Delta_m\stackrel{{\rm def.}}{=} (\mathcal{S}_m,D_m,\omega_m)$ is independent of $m$
and is called the {\em type} of $\boldsymbol{\Delta}$. We will drop the subscript
and write $\Delta\stackrel{{\rm def.}}{=} (\mathcal{S},D,\omega)$ for the type of
$\boldsymbol{\Delta}$.
nodes.section: 4 Scalar-electromagnetic bundles

nodes.name: Electromagnetic bundle
nodes.statement:
Let $\pi\colon (E,h)\to (M,g)$ be a Kaluza-Klein space. An
\emph{electromagnetic bundle} ${\boldsymbol{\Xi}}$ is a duality bundle $\boldsymbol{\Delta}$
over $E$ equipped with a vertical taming $\mathbf{J}$. We write ${\boldsymbol{\Xi}} \stackrel{{\rm def.}}{=}
(\boldsymbol{\Delta},\mathbf{J}) = (\boldsymbol{\mathcal{S}},\boldsymbol{\omega},\mathbf{D},\mathbf{J})$. Let ${\boldsymbol{\Xi}}_{1}$ and ${\boldsymbol{\Xi}}_{2}$
be two electromagnetic bundles. A morphism of electromagnetic bundles
$f\colon {\boldsymbol{\Xi}}_{1}\to {\boldsymbol{\Xi}}_{2}$ from ${\boldsymbol{\Xi}}_{1}$ to ${\boldsymbol{\Xi}}_{2}$ is a
morphism of the underlying duality structures which satisfies $\mathbf{J}_{2}
\circ f = f\circ \mathbf{J}_{1}$.
nodes.section: 4.1 Vertical tamings and scalar-electromagnetic bundles

nodes.name: Scalar-electromagnetic bundle
nodes.statement:
A {\em scalar-electromagnetic bundle} defined over $(M,g)$ is a triple
$\boldsymbol{\mathcal{D}}=(\pi:(E,h)\rightarrow (M,g),\mathbf{\Phi}, {\boldsymbol{\Xi}})$ consisting of a
Kaluza-Klein space $\pi:(E,h)\rightarrow (M,g)$, a vertical potential
$\mathbf{\Phi}$ and an electromagnetic bundle ${\boldsymbol{\Xi}}$ defined over the total
space $E$ of $\pi$. The scalar-electromagnetic bundle $\boldsymbol{\mathcal{D}}$ is called
{\em integrable} if $\pi:(E,h)\rightarrow (M,g)$ is an integrable
Kaluza-Klein space.
nodes.section: 4.1 Vertical tamings and scalar-electromagnetic bundles

nodes.name: Scalar-electromagnetic bundle recovered from one fiber
nodes.statement:
Since $M$ is path-connected, it follows that all fiber
restrictions $(\pi, \mathbf{\Phi}, {\boldsymbol{\Xi}})|_{E_{m}} \stackrel{{\rm def.}}{=}
(E_{m},h_{m},\Phi_{m},\mathcal{S}_m,\omega_m,D_m, J_{m})$ can be recovered by
extended horizontal transport from the 'value' of $\boldsymbol{\mathcal{D}}$ at a fixed
point $m_{0}\in M$.
nodes.section: 4.1 Vertical tamings and scalar-electromagnetic bundles

nodes.name: Fiber scalar-electromagnetic structures D_m
nodes.statement:
In particular, each $\mathcal{D}_m\stackrel{{\rm def.}}{=} (E_m, h_m,
\Phi_m,\mathcal{S}_m,\omega_m,D_m,J_m)$ is a scalar-electromagnetic structure
in the sense of \cite{GESM}.
nodes.section: 4.1 Vertical tamings and scalar-electromagnetic bundles

nodes.name: Type of a scalar-electromagnetic bundle
nodes.statement:
The isomorphism class of $\mathcal{D}_m$ is
independent of $m$ and is called the {\em type} of the
scalar-electromagnetic bundle $\boldsymbol{\mathcal{D}}$. Hence we will drop the subscript
and write $\mathcal{D} \stackrel{{\rm def.}}{=} (\mathcal{M}, \mathcal{G}, \Phi,\mathcal{S},\omega,D,J)$.
nodes.section: 4.1 Vertical tamings and scalar-electromagnetic bundles

nodes.name: Extended holonomy group
nodes.section: 4.1 Vertical tamings and scalar-electromagnetic bundles

nodes.name: Holonomy group independent of base point
nodes.statement:
The holonomy groups associated to $\boldsymbol{\mathcal{D}}$ at different points in $M$
are related by conjugation inside $\mathrm{Aut}(\mathcal{D})$ and hence
isomorphic. Therefore, we can speak of the holonomy group $\mathbb{G}$ of
$\boldsymbol{\mathcal{D}}$ without further reference to base points.
nodes.section: 4.1 Vertical tamings and scalar-electromagnetic bundles

nodes.name: Second projection p^0
nodes.statement: Let $p^0$ be the projection of $E^0$ on the second factor.
nodes.section: 4.2 Topologically trivial scalar-electromagnetic bundles

nodes.name: Existence and uniqueness of the flat connection D^0
nodes.statement:
There exists a unique flat connection $\mathbf{D}^{0}$ on the
pulled-back bundle $\mathcal{S}^{p^0}$ which satisfies the following
conditions for all $e\in E^0$:
\begin{eqnarray}
&& \mathbf{D}^{0}_x(\sigma^{p^0})=0\, , \quad \forall\, \sigma \in \Gamma(\mathcal{M},\mathcal{S})\, , \quad \forall\, x\in H_e(h)\, ,\nonumber\\
&& \mathbf{D}^{0}_x=D^{p^0}_x\, , \quad \forall\, x\in V_{e}\, ,
\end{eqnarray}
where $D^{p^0}$ is the pullback of the connection $D$ through
$p^0$.
nodes.section: 4.2 Topologically trivial scalar-electromagnetic bundles
conclusions:
There exists a unique flat connection $\mathbf{D}^{0}$ on the
pulled-back bundle $\mathcal{S}^{p^0}$

nodes.name: Defining conditions of D^0
nodes.statement:
&& \mathbf{D}^{0}_x(\sigma^{p^0})=0\, , \quad \forall\, \sigma \in \Gamma(\mathcal{M},\mathcal{S})\, , \quad \forall\, x\in H_e(h)\, ,\nonumber\\
&& \mathbf{D}^{0}_x=D^{p^0}_x\, , \quad \forall\, x\in V_{e}\, ,
nodes.section: 4.2 Topologically trivial scalar-electromagnetic bundles

nodes.name: Pulled-back data S^0, J^0, omega^0
nodes.statement:
Let $\boldsymbol{\mathcal{S}}^0\stackrel{{\rm def.}}{=} S^{p^0}$, $\mathbf{J}^0\stackrel{{\rm def.}}{=} J^{p^0}$ and
$\boldsymbol{\omega}^0\stackrel{{\rm def.}}{=} \omega^{p^0}$.
nodes.section: 4.2 Topologically trivial scalar-electromagnetic bundles

nodes.name: Xi^0 is an electromagnetic bundle
nodes.statement:
Then ${\boldsymbol{\Xi}}^{0}\stackrel{{\rm def.}}{=}
(\boldsymbol{\mathcal{S}}^0,\boldsymbol{\omega}^0,\mathbf{D}^{0},\mathbf{J}^0)$ is an electromagnetic bundle defined
over $E^0$ and $\mathbf{\Phi}^0\stackrel{{\rm def.}}{=} \Phi^{p^0}\stackrel{{\rm def.}}{=} \Phi\circ p^0$ is a
vertical potential for $\pi^0$.
nodes.section: 4.2 Topologically trivial scalar-electromagnetic bundles

nodes.name: Horizontally flat sections are pull-backs
nodes.statement:
A section $\boldsymbol{\sigma}\in
\Gamma(E^0,\boldsymbol{\mathcal{S}}^0)$ satisfies $\mathbf{D}^0_X\boldsymbol{\sigma}=0$ for all $X\in
\Gamma(E^0,H)$ if and only if there exists $\sigma\in \Gamma(\mathcal{M},\mathcal{S})$
such that $\boldsymbol{\sigma}=\sigma^{p^0}$.
nodes.section: 4.2 Topologically trivial scalar-electromagnetic bundles

nodes.name: Transport-invariant sections
nodes.statement:
It is easy to see that $\boldsymbol{\sigma}$ is
invariant under the extended horizontal transport $\mathbf{T}^0$ associated
to $H^{0}$ and $\mathbf{D}^0$ if and only if $\sigma$ is invariant under the
action of the subgroup:
\begin{equation*}
{\hat G}^h\stackrel{{\rm def.}}{=} \{{\hat T}^h_\gamma\,\, |\,\, \gamma\in \mathcal{P}(M)\}\subset \mathrm{Isom}(\mathcal{M},\mathcal{G})\, ,
\end{equation*}
where ${\hat T}_\gamma$ was defined in \eqref{hatT}.
nodes.section: 4.2 Topologically trivial scalar-electromagnetic bundles

nodes.name: Topologically trivial scalar-electromagnetic bundle
nodes.statement:
The triple $\boldsymbol{\mathcal{D}}^{0} = (\pi^0:(E^0,h^{0})\rightarrow (M,g),
\mathbf{\Phi}^0,{\boldsymbol{\Xi}}^{0})$ is called a {\em topologically trivial
  scalar-electromagnetic bundle} of type $\mathcal{D}$ defined over $(M,g)$.
nodes.section: 4.2 Topologically trivial scalar-electromagnetic bundles

nodes.name: Metrically trivial scalar-electromagnetic bundle
nodes.statement:
A topologically-trivial scalar-electromagnetic bundle $\boldsymbol{\mathcal{D}}^0$ whose
underlying Kaluza-Klein space $\pi^0:(E^0,h^0)\rightarrow (M,g)$ is
the product Kaluza-Klein bundle (where $h^0=g\times \mathcal{G}$) is called a
{\em metrically trivial} scalar-electromagnetic bundle defined over
$(M,g)$.
nodes.section: 4.2 Topologically trivial scalar-electromagnetic bundles

nodes.name: Invariant sections of metrically trivial bundles
nodes.statement:
For a metrically-trivial scalar-electromagnetic bundle, we have ${\hat
G}=\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal{M}}$. Hence a section $\boldsymbol{\sigma}\in \Gamma(E^0,\boldsymbol{\mathcal{S}}^0)$ is
$\mathbf{T}^0$-invariant if and only if $\boldsymbol{\sigma}=\sigma^{p^0}$ for
some section $\sigma\in \Gamma(\mathcal{M},\mathcal{S})$ of $\mathcal{S}$.
nodes.section: 4.2 Topologically trivial scalar-electromagnetic bundles

nodes.name: Restriction D_alpha
nodes.statement:
Let $\mathcal{D}\stackrel{{\rm def.}}{=}
(\mathcal{M},\mathcal{G},\Phi,\mathcal{S},\omega,D,J)$ be the type of a scalar-electromagnetic
bundle $\boldsymbol{\mathcal{D}}$ and let $\boldsymbol{\mathcal{D}}_\alpha \stackrel{{\rm def.}}{=} (\pi_\alpha,
\mathbf{\Phi}_\alpha,{\boldsymbol{\Xi}}_{\alpha})$ denote its restriction to
$E_\alpha$.
nodes.section: 4.3 Special trivializing atlases for scalar-electromagnetic bundles

nodes.name: Restrictions are scalar-electromagnetic bundles
nodes.statement:
Then $\boldsymbol{\mathcal{D}}_\alpha \stackrel{{\rm def.}}{=} (\pi_\alpha,
\mathbf{\Phi}_\alpha,{\boldsymbol{\Xi}}_{\alpha})$ is a scalar-electromagnetic bundle
defined over $(E_{\alpha},h_{\alpha})$, with Kaluza-Klein metric given
by $h_{\alpha}\stackrel{{\rm def.}}{=} h|_{U_{\alpha}}$.
nodes.section: 4.3 Special trivializing atlases for scalar-electromagnetic bundles

nodes.name: Local trivial model D^0_alpha
nodes.statement:
Let $\boldsymbol{\mathcal{D}}^0_{\alpha}=
(\pi^{0}_{\alpha}, \mathbf{\Phi}^{0}_{\alpha},{\boldsymbol{\Xi}}^{0}_{\alpha})$ be the
topologically trivial scalar-electromagnetic bundle of type $\mathcal{D}$
defined over $E^{0}_\alpha$, with Kaluza-Klein metric $h^{0}_{\alpha}$
making:
\begin{equation*}
q_{\alpha}\colon E_{\alpha}\to U_{\alpha}\times \mathcal{M}\, ,
\end{equation*}
into an isometry (see Subsection \ref{spectriv}).
nodes.section: 4.3 Special trivializing atlases for scalar-electromagnetic bundles

nodes.name: Data of D^0_alpha
nodes.statement:
We have
$\boldsymbol{\mathcal{S}}^0_{\alpha}=\mathcal{S}^{p^0_{\alpha}}$, $\mathbf{D}^0_{\alpha}=D^{p^0_{\alpha}}$,
$\mathbf{J}^0_{\alpha}=J^{p^0_{\alpha}}$, $\boldsymbol{\omega}^0_{\alpha}=\omega^{p^0_{\alpha}}$.
nodes.section: 4.3 Special trivializing atlases for scalar-electromagnetic bundles

nodes.name: Linearized trivializations bold q_alpha
nodes.statement:
The extended horizontal transport $\mathbf{T}$ along geodesics inside
$U_\alpha$ can be used to define unbased isomorphisms of
electromagnetic structures
$\mathbf{q}_\alpha:(\boldsymbol{\mathcal{S}}_\alpha,\boldsymbol{\omega}_\alpha,\mathbf{D}_\alpha,\mathbf{J}_\alpha)\rightarrow
(\boldsymbol{\mathcal{S}}^0_{\alpha}, \boldsymbol{\omega}^0_{\alpha},\mathbf{D}^0_{\alpha}, \mathbf{J}^0_{\alpha})$
which linearize the diffeomorphisms $q_\alpha:E_\alpha\rightarrow
E^0_{\alpha}$ defined in equation \eqref{qalpha}. For any $e\in
E_\alpha$, the linear isomorphism
$\mathbf{q}_{\alpha,e}:\mathcal{S}_e\stackrel{\sim}{\rightarrow}
\mathcal{S}^{p^0_{\alpha}}_{q_\alpha(e)}=\mathcal{S}_{T_{\lambda^{\alpha}\circ\gamma_{\pi(e)}^{\alpha}}(e)}$
is defined through:
\begin{equation*}
\mathbf{q}_{\alpha,e}=\mathbf{T}_{\lambda^{\alpha}\circ\gamma_{\pi(e)}^{\alpha}}(e)\, .
\end{equation*}
nodes.section: 4.3 Special trivializing atlases for scalar-electromagnetic bundles

nodes.section: 4.3 Special trivializing atlases for scalar-electromagnetic bundles

nodes.name: Extended trivializing diagram (ltrivextended)
nodes.section: 4.3 Special trivializing atlases for scalar-electromagnetic bundles
nodes.label: ltrivextended

nodes.name: bold q_alpha is an isomorphism of scalar-electromagnetic structures
nodes.statement:
It is easy to see that $\mathbf{q}_\alpha$ is an
isomorphism of electromagnetic structures from
$(\boldsymbol{\mathcal{S}}_\alpha,\boldsymbol{\omega}_\alpha,\mathbf{D}_\alpha,\mathbf{J}_\alpha)$ to
$(\boldsymbol{\mathcal{S}}^0_{\alpha},\boldsymbol{\omega}^0_{\alpha},\mathbf{D}^0_{\alpha},
\mathbf{J}^0_{\alpha})$. Hence $\mathbf{q}_\alpha$ can be viewed as an isomorphism
of scalar-electromagnetic structures from $\boldsymbol{\mathcal{D}}_\alpha$ to
$\boldsymbol{\mathcal{D}}_{\alpha}^{0}$.
nodes.section: 4.3 Special trivializing atlases for scalar-electromagnetic bundles

nodes.name: Special trivializing atlas of a scalar-electromagnetic bundle
nodes.statement:
By definition, the family
$(U_\alpha,\mathbf{q}_\alpha)_{\alpha\in I}$ is the {\em special trivializing
  atlas} of the scalar-electromagnetic bundle $\boldsymbol{\mathcal{D}}$ defined by the
convex cover $(U_\alpha)_{\alpha\in I}$ and by the data $m_0$ and
$(m^{\alpha},\lambda^{\alpha})_{\alpha\in I}$.
nodes.section: 4.3 Special trivializing atlases for scalar-electromagnetic bundles

nodes.name: Scalar-electromagnetic bundles are locally topologically trivial
nodes.statement:
Since any
scalar-electromagnetic bundle admits such an atlas, it follows that
any scalar-electromagnetic bundle is locally isomorphic with a
topologically trivial scalar-electromagnetic bundle.
nodes.section: 4.3 Special trivializing atlases for scalar-electromagnetic bundles

nodes.name: Unbased automorphisms f_{alpha beta}(m)
nodes.statement:
For any $\alpha,\beta\in I$ such that $U_{\alpha\beta}\neq \emptyset$
and any $m\in U_{\alpha\beta}$, the restriction of the unbased
isomorphism $\mathbf{q}_\beta\circ
\mathbf{q}^{-1}_\alpha:\boldsymbol{\mathcal{S}}^0_{\alpha}|_{E_{\alpha\beta}}\rightarrow
\boldsymbol{\mathcal{S}}^0_{\beta}|_{E_{\alpha\beta}}$ to the fiber $\{m\}\times \mathcal{M}$ can
be identified with the unbased automorphism $\mathbf{f}_{\alpha\beta}(m)\in
\mathrm{Aut}^\mathrm{ub}(\mathcal{S})$ of $\mathcal{S}$ given by:
\begin{equation*}
\mathbf{f}_{\alpha\beta}(m)=\mathbf{T}_{c^{\alpha\beta}_m}\, ,
\end{equation*}
where $c^{\alpha\beta}_m$ is the closed path defined in
\eqref{calphabeta}.
nodes.section: 4.3 Special trivializing atlases for scalar-electromagnetic bundles

nodes.name: f linearizes g
nodes.statement:
This unbased automorphism of $\mathcal{S}$ linearizes the
isometry $\mathbf{g}_{\alpha\beta}(m)\in \mathrm{Iso}(\mathcal{M},\mathcal{G},\Phi)$ of $\mathcal{M}$ given
by the transition function $\mathbf{g}_{\alpha\beta}$.
nodes.section: 4.3 Special trivializing atlases for scalar-electromagnetic bundles

nodes.name: f takes values in Aut(D)
nodes.statement:
Since $\mathbf{J}$ and
$\boldsymbol{\omega}$ and the vertical connection induced by $\mathbf{D}$ are
$\mathbf{T}$-invariant, we have $\mathbf{f}_{\alpha\beta}(m)\in
\mathrm{Aut}(\mathcal{D})=\mathrm{Aut}^\mathrm{ub}_{\mathcal{M},\mathcal{G},\Phi}(\mathcal{S},D,\omega,J)$.
nodes.section: 4.3 Special trivializing atlases for scalar-electromagnetic bundles

nodes.name: Extended transition functions
nodes.statement:
This gives maps
$\mathbf{f}_{\alpha\beta}:U_{\alpha\beta}\rightarrow \mathrm{Aut}(\mathcal{D})$, which we
call the {\em extended transition functions} of the special
trivializing atlas $(U_\alpha,\mathbf{q}_\alpha)_{\alpha\in I}$.
nodes.section: 4.3 Special trivializing atlases for scalar-electromagnetic bundles

nodes.name: Cocycle condition for extended transition functions
nodes.statement:
In
addition, notice that $\mathbf{f}_{\alpha\beta}$ satisfy the cocycle
condition:
\begin{equation} \mathbf{f}_{\beta\gamma}\mathbf{f}_{\alpha\beta}=\mathbf{f}_{\alpha\gamma}\, ,
\end{equation}
which implies the cocycle condition \eqref{gcocycle} for
$\mathbf{g}_{\alpha\beta}$.
nodes.section: 4.3 Special trivializing atlases for scalar-electromagnetic bundles

nodes.name: Cocycle condition (fcocycle)
nodes.statement: \mathbf{f}_{\beta\gamma}\mathbf{f}_{\alpha\beta}=\mathbf{f}_{\alpha\gamma}\, ,
nodes.section: 4.3 Special trivializing atlases for scalar-electromagnetic bundles
nodes.label: fcocycle

nodes.name: Argument: homotopies lift in the integrable case
nodes.statement:
When $\boldsymbol{\mathcal{D}}$ is integrable, any homotopy between paths in $M$ lifts to
a homotopy between the horizontal lifts of those paths in $E$.
nodes.section: 4.3 Special trivializing atlases for scalar-electromagnetic bundles
nodes.statement_short: Homotopies of paths lift to homotopies of horizontal lifts.

nodes.name: Extended transition functions are constant (integrable case)
nodes.statement:
This
implies that the transition functions $\mathbf{f}_{\alpha\beta}$ are constant
on $U_{\alpha\beta}$ and hence they can be viewed as elements of
$\mathrm{Aut}(\mathcal{D})$ which cover $\mathbf{g}_{\alpha\beta}\in \mathrm{Iso}(\mathcal{M},\mathcal{G},\Phi)$.

nodes.name: Transport invariance of Theta and Psi
nodes.statement:
Let us fix $m_{0}\in M$. The fact that the restriction $\Psi_{m_{0}}$
of the fundamental bundle field $\mathbf{\Psi}$ to $E_{m_{0}}$ is a vector
field over $E_{m_{0}}$ taking values on $End(\mathcal{S}_{m_{0}})$ together
with the fact that the extended horizontal transport $\mathbf{T}_{\gamma}$
preserves the flat symplectic connection on $\boldsymbol{\mathcal{S}}$ and covers
isometries, implies:
\begin{equation} \mathbf{T}_{\gamma} \cdot \Theta_{m_{0}} = \Theta_{m}\, , \qquad \forall\, m\in M\, ,
\end{equation}
\begin{equation} \mathbf{T}_{\gamma} \cdot\Psi_{m_{0}} = \Psi_{m}\, , \qquad \forall\, m\in M\, ,
\end{equation}
where $\gamma\in\mathcal{P}(M)$ is a path in $M$ with initial point $\gamma(0)
= m_{0}$ and final point $\gamma(1) = m$.
